newsitem.title: Egypt: Syrian ministers meet Mubarak for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Syrian ministers meet Mubarak for peace talks.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak held almost two hours of talks on Friday with Syria's vice-president and foreign minister about developments in Middle East peace negotiations, government sources said.

Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara did not speak to reporters after the meeting, held on the day that Israeli soldiers pulled out of most of the West Bank town of Hebron after a deal on Palestinian self-rule.

An Egyptian government source said earlier: "The Syrian officials will discuss with President Mubarak developments in the peace process in light of a good and honest implementation of the Hebron deal, which is a step that will open the door to movement on the peace process as a whole."

Khaddam and Shara earlier met Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri to discuss bilateral relations and Arab affairs, the source said. They were expected to spend the night in Cairo and return home on Saturday.

A Syrian spokesman said Mubarak and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad discussed "some Arab issues" by telephone on Thursday and the official Syrian newspaper al-Thawra said on Friday there was nothing new to encourage Syria to resume peace talks with Israel.
Egypt, the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel, and has often mediated behind the scenes between the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours.

Syria has held sporadic talks with Israel since 1991 but the negotiations have been blocked over the fate of the Golan Heights, occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East War. Talks broke off in March last year.
